author: WP20
summary: Explains how to audit CNA's XNA surface against xna4-spec and the reference assemblies, the five-layer reading of the 331/3,627 census, and worked audits of Ray and Viewport. Mostly current, but Ray's boxed Equals now exists, the default Viewport depth range is 0..0, and the TitleSafeArea question is settled by XNA's own IL. The site had the census numbers and the authority rule; the method, the per-category census table and the worked audits are new on a practice deep dive.

sections.heading: Where it sits in CNA's authority hierarchy

concepts.text: TARGET's generated census reports 331/331 public runtime types and 3,627/3,627 documented members represented, and every row carries behavior_assessed false: representation coverage, not behavioural compatibility.

xna4-spec converts Microsoft's XNA 4.0 reference pages into 544 XML type files in 19 namespace directories, each with kind, syntax, members, overloads, parameters, returns, remarks and platform lists; it includes build-time namespaces.

target.evidence: xna4-spec @fedc17aa (index.xml: 544 <type> entries; 545 .xml files incl. index); XML identical to @8f61207

concepts.text: xna4-spec's README says 550 types while its index, table and files say 544, a small drift showing that even a machine-readable conversion must be validated as data.
The converted text remains Microsoft's documentation, offered by the repository for informational and educational use.

concepts.section: Where it sits in CNA's authority hierarchy
concepts.text: No file in CNA references xna4-spec; CNA's CHECKLIST.md names the XNA reference assemblies as authority for API surface and FNA for behaviour, with real XNA and oracles settling what documentation cannot.

target.evidence: CHECKLIST.md (API surface section); git grep for xna4-spec at 009d40f5 (no hits, per ecosystem page)

concepts.section: Where it sits in CNA's authority hierarchy
concepts.text: xna4-spec is a complementary inventory: it can expose members FNA omitted, supply remarks for review and make audits scriptable, but it cannot prove CNA behaviour and a clean comparison against it is not a CNA gate.
Read the closure through five layers: header representation, exact/semantic/host classification, implemented behaviour, tested behaviour, and renderer/platform-dependent behaviour.
tokens: Read the closure through five layers

concepts.text: The census classifies 1,746 members exact, 1,823 semantic and 58 host-language substitutions with none missing, not applicable or needing review; per category properties are 1,039 semantic and 1 substitution.
A member can be represented perfectly and still hide a bug, a bounded refusal or an untested renderer route (e.g. Effect(GraphicsDevice&, bytes) refused on 11 identities).
tokens: represented perfectly and still contain a bug

target.evidence: site canonical facts (compiled effects on 14 of 25 identities)

concepts.text: A disciplined one-type audit has six steps: pin revisions, extract structured members, map C# idioms, compare and classify each row, read hand-written implementations, and attach an executable oracle.

The idiom mapping table is part of the result: without it Equals(object) looks missing and a default constructor or iterator looks like an unmarked extension; CHECKLIST.md lists the accepted equivalents.
tokens: The mapping table is part of the result

concepts.text: Ray has 16 documented members; CNA's header declares both fields, default and two-vector constructors, two Equals overloads, GetHashCode, four value-returning Intersects, three output-reference forms, ToString and free equality operators; the census rates 11 exact and 5 semantic.
Claim that CNA omits boxed Equals(Object): at TARGET Ray has Equals(const std::any&) (added by XNA-MISSING-002); GetHashCode returns std::size_t and XORs the vector hashes where XNA adds them.
concepts.note: Corrected: boxed Equals exists; added the hash-combination difference found by reading both implementations.

target.evidence: modules/math/src/Ray.cpp (Equals, GetHashCode); commit 37f42e2e7; XNA IL Ray::GetHashCode (add)

concepts.text: xna4-spec's Ray.xml lists each output Intersects overload twice (a Windows Phone record with Nullable<Single> and an Xbox 360/Windows record with Nullable<float>) and records op_Equality() without parameters; compare against reference member IDs, not signature strings.
concepts.note: Corrected: the duplicates are per-platform records; the Bible's 'wrong target type' labels were not reproduced and are not repeated.

concepts.text: Viewport has 14 documented members (two constructors, nine properties, Project, Unproject, ToString): 5 exact and 9 semantic; CNA uses DEF_PROP for six properties and hand-writes AspectRatio, Bounds and TitleSafeArea.

Claim that the default Viewport has a 0-to-1 depth range: at TARGET every field is zero (MaxDepth 0), matching XNA's struct default; the two constructors set MinDepth 0 and MaxDepth 1 as XNA's do, and AspectRatio returns 0 for a zero dimension like XNA.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna/Viewport.cpp (constructors, getAspectRatioProperty); XNA 4.0 Graphics IL (Viewport .ctor, get_AspectRatio)

concepts.text: TitleSafeArea returns Bounds, pinned by ViewportTest.TitleSafeAreaEqualsBounds; the genuine XNA 4.0 Windows assembly also returns the bounds unchanged, so CNA matches Windows XNA while Xbox 360 behaviour is undecided by that assembly.
concepts.note: Resolved the Bible's open question with the IL: a sourced match, not a deviation.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/tests/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/ViewportTests.cpp (TitleSafeAreaEqualsBounds); XNA IL Viewport::GetTitleSafeArea returns new Rectangle(x,y,w,h)

concepts.text: The right outcome of such an audit is a recorded, sourced behaviour or deviation, not a surface percentage; hand-written properties deserve the most scrutiny.

An API inventory cannot establish run-time defaults, float edges, exception type and timing, lifetime, GPU state, wire compatibility, content decoding, platform substitution, or whether a member is a stub, a refusal or complete.
tokens: stub, a safe refusal or a complete implementation

concepts.text: Use xna4-spec for questions, the strict CNAEXT build for unmarked additions, reference XML and IL for surface and Windows behaviour, FNA/XNA runs for semantics and the oracle hierarchy for verdicts, without collapsing them into one number.

issues.text: The API census asserts representation only (behavior_assessed false on all 3,627 rows) and is a manual script, not a CI gate.
Viewport.TitleSafeArea returning Bounds matches the Windows XNA 4.0 assembly; Ray.GetHashCode XOR vs XNA add is an unspecified hash value.
